item.title: Australia quietly revives Antarctic logistics pact with China as ties steady
item.description: Australia has quietly revived a bilateral Antarctic logistics pact with China, as the two countries work to put bilateral ties on a stable footing despite lingering security tensions. item.title: Myanmar’s Asean exit talk: a pariah pushes back
item.description: For five years, one name card has been missing from the grand circular table at the Association of Southeast Asean Nations biannual leaders’ summit: Min Aung Hlaing. As president of Myanmar, he should by diplomatic convention sit alongside the 10 other leaders of the Southeast Asian bloc at its regular get-togethers. item.title: Son of Hamas chief survived Israeli strike, group says
item.description: The son of Hamas ⁠chief Khalil al-Hayya survived an assassination attempt ⁠by the Israeli military on Friday, senior Hamas official ⁠Basem Naim said. He said that Izzeldeen al-Hayya and his family had survived a dawn air strike and Hamas sources said several people, including Hayya’s daughter-in-law, had been wounded but there had been no deaths. item.title: Colombian Congress chiefs rush to reassure Beijing as envoy berates lawmakers in Taiwan
item.description: Colombian congressional leaders lined up to reaffirm the one-China policy in meetings with Beijing’s ambassador, as nine lawmakers neared the end of a trip to Taiwan that Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella has yet to comment on. item.title: Taiwan is expanding its military draft. Will those troops make a difference?
item.description: Taiwan’s move to toughen up on exemptions to military service has sparked anxiety among some young men facing conscription and raised questions over whether expanding recruitment will actually strengthen the island’s combat readiness.
